issue_context.title: Wrong nullable annotations on IHubProtocol.TryParseMessage in SignalR
issue_context.body: The interface [IHubProtocol](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v5.0.1/src/SignalR/common/SignalR.Common/src/Protocol/IHubProtocol.cs#L38) should have `HubMessage?` type for its `out` parameter `message`. Existing implementations like [JsonHubProtocol](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v5.0.1/src/SignalR/common/Protocols.Json/src/Protocol/JsonHubProtocol.cs#L91), [MessagePackHubProtocol](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v5.0.1/src/SignalR/common/Protocols.MessagePack/src/Protocol/MessagePackHubProtocol.cs#L64) return null from this method.

review_comments:
Could this result in a NullReferenceException? Given that the caller acquires the connection lock after calling OnServerTimeout, it sure looks like it could.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5c0693f9418788e59a5d70dab9536719a84aff00/src/SignalR/clients/csharp/Client.Core/src/HubConnection.cs#L1850-L1857

Any method that references CurrentConnectionStateUnsynchronized without locking because it assumed the caller did so on it's behalf should have `Unsynchronized` in its name and probably call `_state.AssertInConnectionLock()`.
Nvm. The comment was right about it being only called from tests. There are multiple OnServerTimeout() methods in the same file. This and the one it's calling.
Is this a change from .NET 5? There is an aspnetcore annoucement issue for nullability changes.
This is an API change, however passing null would have thrown
Huh, weird that `TextWriter.Write(char[])` allows a nullable array.

I don't think so? That would force callers to always handle null even if they never expect it to be null. If they use a nullable for `TResult` then that means they expect a null value and should handle it, and the compiler will let them know that. So seems better to let the user decide.
Fair enough. It's effectively the same choice we made with JSInterop. But we also do not provide any guarantees against it which is crummy.
No it isn't, we check above that the token type is a string. If the string is null it would have token type null.
Would it be better to throw if there's no ConnectionId in the negotiate response?
Hmm, I wonder if there is a better way to avoid all these bangs.
Should ConnectionId be made nullable on ConnectionContext?

I really think that people should be able to rely on `ConnectionContext.ConnectionId` being non-null. I'm thinking this should just throw if someone tries to access this property before `StartAsync()` completes.

This implementation of `ConnectionContext.ConnectionId` is already a bit odd in that its setter throws, so I don't think throwing from the getter when the connection hasn't started is a big deal.

> people should be able to rely on `ConnectionContext.ConnectionId` being non-null

It's not just if you access it before starting, if you skip negotiation then this will be null as well.
